Email

Copy Link

A file photo of US President Donald Trump | Reuters/ANI

Stay updated with ThePrint:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

-->

New Delhi: Donald Trump is now a lame duck. He has lost power in the Congress. The blue sweep of Democrats in the US midterm elections has clipped the 80-year-old president’s ability to advance his domestic agenda while raising questions about how he will use the powers he retains for the remainder of his four-year term.

Unlike a first-term president, Trump cannot seek re-election. With no further campaign to fight, and his party now weakened, he has officially entered what is commonly known as a lame-duck period: A stretch in which a president’s political influence is diminished, even as the formal powers of the office remain intact.

With Democrats set to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in January, the shift could have consequences well beyond Washington.

Show Full Article

Trump will face a Congress capable of blocking legislation, investigating his administration and scrutinising the decisions behind his policies. But the presidency retains considerable authority over foreign affairs, particularly the use of military force. That imbalance could make the next two years unpredictable.

Trump struck a surprisingly conciliatory tone after the Democrat victories, congratulating the party and saying he was prepared to work with its leaders. How long that willingness will last is uncertain. He has also reminded Democrats that he retains the power to veto legislation, even posting an image of a red baseball cap bearing the word “VETO”.

But there is no denying that Republican influence is on a downslide. Kansas elected a Democratic senator for the first time since 1932, while Texas elected one for the first time since 1988. South Carolina’s Darline Graham failed to retain the seat held by her late brother, Republican powerbroker Lindsey Graham. Iowa, long regarded as a Republican stronghold, also elected a Democratic senator.

Trump has experienced a lame duck period before, between November 2020 and January 2021, after losing the presidential election to Joe Biden.

Rather than oversee a conventional transfer of power, he sought to overturn the result despite clear evidence of Biden’s victory. He is the first US president in a century to serve two non-consecutive terms, making him the only president in living memory to face a second lame-duck period—one that could last more than two years.

Trump’s second lame-duck period A lame-duck president is generally one who no longer has to contend with another election. The expression has an older history. It was first used in the 18th century to describe a stockbroker unable to meet his debts, before entering the American political lexicon in the 19th century to describe defeated or politically weakened officeholders.

In the United States, the period between an election and the inauguration of newly-elected officials came to be known as the lame-duck period. The Twentieth Amendment, ratified in 1933, shortened that transition by moving the start of a new Congress to January 3 and the presidential inauguration to January 20.

Second-term presidents, however, are not necessarily powerless. Freed from the need to campaign, they can sometimes take politically difficult decisions or pursue diplomatic initiatives that might have been harder to attempt earlier. The absence of electoral pressure can make them more willing to take risks abroad, even as their domestic political capital declines.

There is precedent. At the end of his presidency, Bill Clinton made an intensive effort to secure an Israeli-Palestinian settlement and explored a presidential visit to North Korea.

After Democrats won the 2014 midterm elections, Barack Obama concluded the Iran nuclear agreement and moved to normalise relations with Cuba. George H. W. Bush sent US forces to Somalia in late 1992 on a limited mission to help ease famine. In 2007, after a punishing midterm defeat, George W. Bush ordered a troop surge in Iraq in an attempt to stabilise the country.

The outcomes were mixed. Clinton’s peace efforts failed, and Obama’s diplomatic achievements proved short-lived. The Somalia intervention helped avert hunger but left the underlying conflict unresolved; a subsequent expansion of the mission under Clinton had disastrous consequences. Bush’s Iraq surge reduced violence in the short term but did little to secure lasting stability.

Those initiatives, however, were debated with government officials and outside experts, and their objectives were clearly articulated, even when they were not achieved. Trump, by contrast, has often failed to explain or justify his foreign policy decisions.

The risks beyond Congress With Democrats preparing to investigate his administration and his family’s business dealings, Trump could become more combative, according to reports. Congress may be able to summon officials, demand documents and hold hearings, but it has fewer tools to control the President’s day-to-day conduct of foreign policy.

There are several ways Trump could retaliate or seek to reassert his authority: Issuing fresh threats against Canada, undermining US alliances or reaching an understanding with Russia or China at the expense of Ukraine or Taiwan. Of course, turning such threats into policy would require more sustained diplomatic or military effort, including troop movements and negotiations with other powers.

The more immediate concerns are Iran and Cuba. According to The New York Times , the Trump administration and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the midterms. A further attempt to force Tehran into submission is unlikely to succeed, the report argues, and could threaten the global economy as well as the security of US allies in the Persian Gulf.

The war with Iran has already become a central issue in the midterm campaign. Disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has contributed to rising prices, angering voters who had heard Trump promise during the 2024 presidential campaign that he would not start new wars.

Democrats have repeatedly argued that Trump had no authority to launch the war without congressional approval. They have invoked the War Powers Resolution in attempts to force the administration to seek authorisation or end US military involvement. With control of Congress, they will be able to call administration officials to testify under oath and investigate how the war was planned and conducted.

Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth is likely to face questions about the cost of the conflict, the intelligence used to justify the decision to attack Iran and the number of missile interceptors remaining in the US arsenal. Lawmakers may also examine how Washington intends to protect its Gulf allies and the role Israel played in persuading Trump to launch the war.

Trump could nevertheless decide to escalate. He appears to believe that intensifying the conflict might break the stalemate and improve his legacy. But Iranian leaders are unlikely to retreat under greater military pressure. They could instead intensify attacks on commercial shipping and Gulf allies, while refusing diplomatic overtures until Trump leaves office, a Foreign Policy article argues.

Trump has suggested that he still wants a negotiated end to the conflict. In an interview with Fox News Tuesday after the election, he said he was seeking a deal, but added: “Otherwise I’ll just finish the job.”

Cuba presents another possible target. The administration has imposed a sweeping embargo on the island for much of 2026, seeking to weaken its government. Cut off from Venezuelan support and facing electricity shortages that leave residents with power for only a few hours a day, Cuba has experienced worsening economic hardship and human suffering.

Secretary of State and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio has made removing the Cuban government a personal priority. Such a move would also fit with Trump’s so-called “Donroe Doctrine”, an assertion of US primacy in the western hemisphere.

A president with other priorities Foreign policy is not the only arena in which Trump can still exercise power. He has repeatedly threatened to use executive orders to advance his hardline immigration agenda, as he did during the first months of his second term. He can also veto legislation passed by a Democrat-controlled Congress and challenge investigations into his administration.

There is also the possibility that Trump will turn his attention away from foreign policy and towards his own financial interests. His family has already benefited from business arrangements involving foreign entities, including a jetliner gifted by Qatar’s emir, a $2 billion investment from a fund led by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and profits from cryptocurrency ventures that have attracted foreign buyers. The New Yorker has estimated that the Trump family has made $4 billion through such activities.

Or Trump might not make any foreign policy decisions and focus on his beautification dreams.

He has shown considerable interest in reshaping Washington, DC, as a monument to his presidency. His plans include redecorating the Oval Office, building a $400 million ballroom in the White House, renovating the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and remodelling the Kennedy Centre. The ballroom is expected to be completed in late 2028, shortly before he leaves office.

In his closing speech before the midterm elections, Trump spent little time discussing policy and instead spoke about his plans to beautify the Capital. He could spend much of his remaining time issuing pardons, pursuing political opponents and building monuments to himself.

As The National noted, “The lame duck may have lost a lot of his political bite, but he is not yet ready to fly south for the winter.”

(Edited by Viny Mishra)

item.title: アングル：米中間選挙の民主勝利、市場に新たな波乱 外交・財政リスク警戒
item.description:
Dhara Ranasinghe Ankur Banerjee
[ロンドン ４日 ロイター] - 米中間選挙での民主党...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アングル：米中間選挙の民主勝利、市場に新たな波乱　外交・財政リスク警戒 0:29 配信

2026年11月1日、米国ワシントンD.C.の米国議会議事堂　REUTERS/Umit Bektas（ロイター） Dhara Ranasinghe　Ankur Banerjee

[ロンドン ４日 ロイター] - 米中間選挙での民主党の圧勝は、市場にとって新たな波乱要因となった。市場は既に、イラン戦争の余波に加え、成長とインフレを押し上げてきたＡＩ（人工知能）ブーム、そして米国の債務拡大への対応に追われている。

投資家は市場の変動が続くとみて身構えている。特に２つの分野に注目が集まっている。今年に入り原油価格を７０％押し上げてきたイラン戦争の行方と、米国の財政支出を巡る激しい論争だ。

約６０００億ドルの資産を運用するＲＢＣブルーベイ・アセット・マネジメントのマーケット戦略責任者マイク・ベル氏は「市場にとって最大の潜在的な影響は、中間選挙という障害がなくなった今、トランプ大統領が中東でのエスカレーションに踏み切ると決断した場合だろう。エスカレーションが続きエネルギー価格が上昇すれば、株式と債券が同時に打撃を受ける可能性がある」と語った。

イラン戦争が続く中、原油価格は１バレル＝１００ドルを超える水準で高止まりし、消費者や企業の燃料コストを押し上げている。一方、中央銀行は、より大幅な利上げを迫られるような広範な物価急騰への波及リスクに警戒を強めている。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は、５年以上にわたってインフレ目標を達成できていない。ユーロ圏でも、１０月のインフレ率はエネルギー高を背景に４％と３年ぶりの高水準に上昇した。今後数カ月でさらに上がる見通しだ。これにより、１２月の欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）の利上げを巡る市場の観測が改めて裏付けられた。

アナリストによると、トランプ氏が外交政策の主導権を握り続けるため、地政学的リスクは引き続き高いという。

イラン戦争に加え、今年は、米国によるベネズエラのマドゥロ大統領の拘束や、デンマーク自治領グリーンランドを巡ってトランプ氏が欧州の同盟国に関税で脅しをかけたことも、投資家の不意を突いた。

ベレンベルクのチーフエコノミスト、ホルガー・シュミーディング氏は「トランプ政権の残り２年間は、外交政策を巡る大きな混乱に備えなければならないだろう」と述べた。

＜ＡＩ投資から債務へ＞

民主党の勝利を受けて規制面での監視強化がＡＩ分野の急成長を妨げかねないとの懸念が、市場の当面の焦点となった。

世論調査では、民主党支持者がＡＩへの規制強化を支持していることが示されており、投資家は民主党が多数派を占める議会が同分野への監視を強めると予想している。

プリンシパル・アセット・マネジメントのチーフグローバルストラテジスト、シーマ・シャー氏は「ＡＩは米国の成長ストーリーの極めて重要な部分を占めている。だから、どの政党が政権を握ろうとも、投資の拡大を支えつつコスト面の懸念に配慮するという、両方のいいとこ取りを目指すだろう」と述べた。同氏は、第２次世界大戦終結以降、Ｓ＆Ｐ株価指数が中間選挙の１年後にはいずれの場合も上昇していると指摘した。

それでも投資家は、市場の底堅さについて神経質になってきている。ＡＩの設備投資急増と多額の債務を抱える政府が、金利を数十年ぶりの高水準に押し上げ、市場の弱点を露呈させてきた。

シャー氏は、選挙結果を受けて一段と制約を受ける可能性がある財政政策の行方を注視すると付け加えた。

アナリストからは、共和党が勝利した場合に米成人に５０００ドルの小切手を配るというトランプ氏の公約が実現しないことへの安堵が示された。

ソシエテ・ジェネラルの新興国リサーチ世界責任者フェニックス・カレン氏は、民主党が議会を支配すれば、財政政策への監視が強まり、トランプ氏が支出拡大の面でできることに歯止めがかかる公算が大きいと指摘。「それは財政政策により厳しい制約を課すものであり、米国債利回りへの圧力を幾分和らげる助けになるはずだ」と語った。

４０兆ドルを超える米国の債務残高への懸念は、今年の国債利回りを押し上げる一因となってきた。

議会は２０２７会計年度の支出を巡る激しい論争を中間選挙後に先送りしており、資金調達合意に達するための期限を１２月１１日に設定した。

債務上限引き上げの期限は２０２７年後半まで到来しない見通しだが、民主党はいわゆる「Ｘデート」を、支出・税制政策を巡る共和党との交渉の切り札として使える可能性がある。借り入れ上限への対応に向けた賛成票と引き換えに、譲歩を迫るものだ。

シャー氏は「市場の変動は続くとみている。今後１年は手に汗握る展開になるだろう」と述べた。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米10月ＩＳＭ非製造業指数、54.5へ小幅低下　投入価格高止まり 0:02 配信

10月31日、米ニューハンプシャー州デリーにあるレストランで撮影。REUTERS/Kylie Cooper（ロイター） [ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - 米供給管理協会（ＩＳＭ）が４日発表した１０月の非製造業購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）は５４．５と、前月の５４．９から小幅に低下した。新規事業の勢いが鈍化した。一方、供給網の混乱は続き、投入価格は高止まりした。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は５４．８だった。

ＰＭＩは第４・四半期の米経済が堅調な滑り出しとなったことを示した。ただ、エコノミストは景気の減速を予想している。個人消費は２四半期続けて力強く伸びたが、今後は減速するとみられている。高インフレが家計の購買力を圧迫しており、消費を抑える一因になるとみられる。

１０月の新規事業指数は５５．９と、９月の５９．８から低下した。イラン戦争や輸入関税の影響で、供給業者の納入状況は一段と悪化した。

供給業者の納入状況を示す指数は５６．７と、９月の５３．２から大幅に上昇した。５０を上回ると納入の遅れを示す。納入の遅れは２３カ月連続となり、投入価格の高止まりにつながっている。

投入コストを示す支払価格指数は７３．０と、９月の７４．０から低下したものの、なお高水準だった。

雇用指数は５０．１から５１．４へ上昇した。

item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場・序盤＝大幅高、民主勝利で政策転換懸念後退　データセンター株は下落 11/4 23:48 配信

2026年10月30日、ニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）　 REUTERS/Brendan McDermid/File Photo（ロイター） ［ニューヨーク　４日　ロイター］ - 米中間選挙から一夜明けた４日の米国株式市場は、大幅高で寄り付いた。投資家は、中間選挙での民主党の圧勝で「ねじれ」状態となった議会では急激な政策転換が抑えられるとの見方を織り込んだ。

ただ、ＡＩ（人工知能）規制強化への懸念が重しとなり、データセンター関連株は売り圧力にさらされた。

民主党は、ＡＩ業界の急拡大に対する住民の反発が強まっているテキサス州やジョージア州など、主要なデータセンター集積州で議席を伸ばした。

ゴールドマン・サックスのエコノミストはリポートで「州・地方レベルでの民主党の勝利は、短期的にはデータセンター建設の一時停止につながる可能性が高く、米国で計画されているデータセンター容量拡張の約４５％に影響を及ぼす恐れがある」と指摘した。

item.title: 米9月貿易赤字、0.7％減の1050億ドル 輸入は過去最高
item.description: [ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - 米商務省が４日発表した９月の貿易赤字（季節調整済み）は前月比０．７％減の１０５０億ド...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米9月貿易赤字、0.7％減の1050億ドル　輸入は過去最高 11/4 23:10 配信

8月10日、米ニュージャージー州ニューアーク港で撮影。REUTERS/Jordan Tovin（ロイター） [ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - 米商務省が４日発表した９月の貿易赤字（季節調整済み）は前月比０．７％減の１０５０億ドルとなった。堅調な内需を背景に輸入が過去最高を記録したものの、赤字幅はわずかに縮小した。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は１０８０億ドルだった。

今回の報告では、トランプ大統領による積極的な関税政策にもかかわらず、メキシコ、ベトナム、台湾、韓国など複数の国との財（モノ）の貿易赤字が過去最高を記録したことも示された。

９月の輸入は１．２％増の４２６６億ドルと過去最高を記録した。モノの輸入は１．３％増の３４６９億ドルと、こちらも過去最高となった。ＡＩ基盤の構築に伴い、コンピューターや同関連機器の輸入が増えたことが背景に、資本財の輸入は１１６億ドル増の１５８０億ドルと過去最高を記録した。半導体の輸入は１２億ドル減少した。

消費財の輸入は２４億ドル増加。医薬品が２９億ドル増加したことが寄与した。工業用資材・原材料の輸入は３７億ドル減少。非貨幣用金と原油の減少を反映した。非貨幣用金は国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）の算定から除外される。石油を除く輸入は過去最高となった。

サービスの輸入は、旅行・輸送サービスの増加を背景に、８億ドル増の７９７億ドルと過去最高を記録した。

輸出は１．９％増の３２１５億ドル。モノの輸出は２．５％増の２１１０億ドルとなった。資本財の輸出は３８億ドル増の７３３億ドルと過去最高を記録。コンピューター・同関連機器、民間航空機がけん引した。

食品・飲料の輸出は１９億ドル増の１６０億ドルと、２０２２年６月以来の高水準となった。原油の輸出は１２億ドル増加した。 一方、工業用資材・原材料の輸出は非貨幣用金の減少を受けて落ち込んだ。

サービスの輸出は７億ドル増の１１０５億ドルと、過去最高となった。旅行サービスと知的財産使用の増加が押し上げた。

トランプ大統領による積極的な関税政策にもかかわらず、貿易赤字は大幅な水準にとどまっている。米商務省が先週発表した第３・四半期の国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）速報値によると、輸入は第３・四半期のＧＤＰ成長率を２．６４％ポイント押し下げた。

３日投開票の米中間選挙では、不人気な対イラン戦争への強い不満や生活費高騰への不安、トランプ大統領の政権運営に対する怒りを背景に、民主党が上下両院の過半数を奪還した。内需は底堅い個人消費と、企業による人工知能（ＡＩ）への活発な投資が押し上げている。データセンター建設への反対も、共和党の選挙敗北の一因となった。

キャピタル・エコノミクスのシニア北米エコノミスト、トーマス・ライアン氏は「ＡＩの拡充を支えるためのこうしたモノの大量輸入が、貿易赤字を現在の過去最高に近い水準まで拡大させた主因だ」と指摘。その上で「ただ、前夜に全米各地の知事選でＡＩ懐疑派が相次いで勝利したことを踏まえると、このペースが今後も続くかどうかには疑問符が付く」と述べた。

ロイター 関連リンク アングル：米移民摘発、過去最高の逮捕件数も送還難航　法的手続きや移送能力に壁 コラム：米財務省の借入拡大、債務問題の大きさに比べれば単なるノイズ 焦点：テスラ、ロボタクシー「サイバーキャブ」で試す規制の限界 コラム：日銀利上げの「美しいシナリオ」に弱点はないか＝上野泰也氏 コラム：日米協調介入が告げる円高への転換、円安派は今こそ見直しの時 11/5(木) 1:13 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: China Seeks Extradition of Five Uyghurs From Thailand
item.description: Thailand will allow five Uyghur men to challenge a Chinese extradition request in court before approving their deportation, a Thai government spokesman said, with human rights groups warning they face the risk of torture if sent back. The men were among 300 Uyghurs, a persecuted …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
Thailand will allow five Uyghur men to challenge a Chinese extradition request in court before approving their deportation, a Thai government spokesman said, with human rights groups warning they face the risk of torture if sent back.

The men were among 300 Uyghurs, a persecuted minority numbering around 10 million in the western region of Xinjiang, who fled to the Southeast Asian country in 2014, where they were detained for illegal entry.

The five Uyghurs were later prosecuted for escaping detention. Two are now nearing the end of their sentences, government spokesperson Ekkapob Pianpises told Reuters on Wednesday.

“The Thai government has granted them the right to contest the case,” Ekkapob said, adding the two men had been appointed a lawyer and the courts would decide their challenge.

The three others still have to spend another year in Thai jail for their escape attempt, General Chaiyapruek Duangprapat, secretary-general of the National Security Council, told reporters on Wednesday.

Hundreds, possibly thousands, of Uyghurs fled unrest in China’s western Xinjiang region in 2014, following a wave of violent attacks that prompted a massive crackdown by Chinese authorities. Rights groups and the UN have accused Beijing of abuses against the Uyghur minority, including the mass use of forced labour in internment camps.Beijing denies any abuses.

Asked about the extradition request of the five Uyghurs, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told reporters that China and Thailand’s cooperation in tackling cross-border crimes such as human smuggling was in line with both countries’ laws, international law and practice.

Thailand and China signed an extradition treaty in 1993 that entered into force in 1999, but requests under the pact must go through Thai courts.

Human rights groups urged Thailand to halt the extradition, saying the men faced a grave risk of torture and other abuses in China.

“Previous Thai governments have kept Uyghurs in inhumane detention for years and then complied with Beijing’s demands to send them to China, where they were forcibly disappeared,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch.

Thailand sent nearly 100 of the Uyghurs arrested in 2014 back to China the following year, drawing widespread condemnation, while a group of more than 170 were identified as Turkish citizens and sent to Turkey.

Some diplomats and security analysts have linked that deportation to the bombing of a Bangkok shrine a month later that killed 20 people.

Thailand then deported another 40 Uyghurs from the same group to China in February 2025 despite appeals from United Nations human rights experts to halt their return.

item.title: Sebi eases digital KYC rules for NRIs, foreign nationals from December 3
item.description: Sebi will allow NRIs, OCIs and foreign nationals in FATF-compliant countries to complete KYC digitally from December 3, easing onboarding and investment in Indian markets ...
item.dc:creator: Khushboo Tiwari
item.content:encoded: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Wednesday relaxed know-your-customer (KYC) requirements for persons resident outside India (PROIs), allowing those in Financial Action Task Force (FATF)-compliant countries to complete digital onboarding without being physically present in India. The revised framework, effective December 3, will cover non-resident Indians (NRIs), overseas citizens of India (OCIs), and foreign nationals. Clients residing in FATF non-compliant countries will continue to follow existing KYC requirements. The move aims to ease onboarding and thereby investments by such investors in the Indian markets.  Under the revised norms, intermediaries can accept digital submission of KYC information and supporting documents from eligible clients. The regulator has also made KYC records portable, allowing them to be shared across intermediaries irrespective of whether all individual attributes have been validated. Intermediaries can rely on KYC undertaken by another Sebi-registered intermediary or an entity regulated by another financial sector regulator, based on records obtained from KYC Registration Agencies (KRAs) or the Central KYC Records Registry. The framework requires intermediaries to collect passport copies and, where applicable, OCI cards. Overseas addresses will be accepted as proof of address. Clients can submit KYC forms digitally or physically, while specimen signatures can be submitted electronically, subject to verification during video-based in-person verification. Sebi has mandated the presence of an authorised official during video verification and subjected the process to concurrent audit. Intermediaries will remain ultimately responsible for client KYC, including enhanced due diligence based on risk profiles. Intermediaries must provide completed KYC information to KRAs within three working days. The revised provisions will also apply to re-KYC of clients in FATF-compliant countries.

item.description:
Pete Schroeder
[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - 米通貨監督庁（ＯＣＣ）は４日、大手銀行による人工知...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ＯＣＣ、銀行のＡＩ利用で監督指針　他のリスクと区別せず 11/4 20:35 配信

米通貨監督庁（ＯＣＣ）のロゴ REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration（ロイター） Pete Schroeder

[ワシントン ４日 ロイター] - 米通貨監督庁（ＯＣＣ）は４日、大手銀行による人工知能（ＡＩ）利用の監督指針を出した。検査官に対しＡＩを他のリスクと区別して扱わないよう求めた。

ロイターが確認した文書によると、ＯＣＣがこうした指針を出すのは初めて。

この新たな枠組みでは、ＯＣＣは銀行にＡＩ利用について個別のリスク基準の設定を求めず、検査官もＡＩを特有のリスクとして扱うべきではないとした。ただし、検査官は銀行のＡＩ利用方法に加え、銀行の規模や複雑さを考慮すべきだという。

指針には規則のような法的拘束力はないが、銀行は通常こうした指針に厳格に従う。

ＯＣＣは、検査官が重視すべきなのは銀行の利用する個々のモデルの高度さではなく、ＡＩが誤りを起こした場合の影響だとした。

取引を開始する権限を与えられた単純なＡＩエージェントは、行内向けに使う高度なモデルよりもリスクが高いとみなされ得ると説明した。リスクの高いＡＩ利用では、自律的に動作できる範囲をより厳しく制限したり、人間がより直接的に監督したりする必要が生じる場合があるとしている。

item.title: テンセント、新ＡＩ「ＨＹ４」公開 サイバー攻撃リスク抑制
item.description: ［４日 ロイター］ - 中国の騰訊控股（テンセント）は４日、新たなオープンソースのＡＩ（人工知能）モデル「Ｈｙ４」を...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
テンセント、新ＡＩ「ＨＹ４」公開　サイバー攻撃リスク抑制 11/4 19:56 配信

テンセントのロゴ REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo（ロイター） ［４日　ロイター］ - 中国の騰訊控股（テンセント）は４日、新たなオープンソースのＡＩ（人工知能）モデル「Ｈｙ４」を公開した。サイバー攻撃に悪用されるリスクを減らすため、サイバーセキュリティー関連の学習データを「防御的」な内容に絞ったという。

世界各地でＡＩを利用したサイバー攻撃が相次ぎ、高度なＡＩモデルの能力や、世界のインターネットインフラに与える脅威への懸念が高まっている。

テンセントは、Ｈｙ４が持ち得る「攻撃的」な能力を抑えるため、学習の段階でエクスプロイト（脆弱性を突く攻撃コード）の開発、リバースエンジニアリング、ペネトレーションテスト（侵入テスト）などの内容を取り除いたと説明した。

「高度なサイバー能力や生物学的能力がもたらし得る安全上のリスクを認識している。モデルの学習、オープンソース化、公開において、より責任ある取り組み方を徹底していく」と述べた。

中国のＡＩ企業の間でも、ＡＩが制御不能になるリスクを防ぐ取り組みが見られる。ムーンショットＡＩ（月之暗面）は１０月、最新モデルのサイバー攻撃能力を制限した。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ユーロ圏の賃金、27年にやや上昇加速へ＝ＥＣＢ 11/4 19:47 配信

フランクフルトのECB本部、3月19日撮影 REUTERS/Jana Rodenbusch（ロイター） ［フランクフルト　４日　ロイター］ - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）は４日、最新の賃金協定に基づくと、ユーロ圏の賃金上昇率が２０２７年１─９月にやや加速するとの予想を示した。

ＥＣＢの賃金トラッカーの総合指標は、有効な労働協約を対象とし、一時金を１２カ月で平準化して算出する。この指標によると、今年下半期の賃金上昇率は２．７％。２７年第３・四半期には２．４％に低下する見通し。ただ、ＥＣＢはサンプルが限られていると注意を促した。

一時金を除いた賃金トラッカーによると、２６年が２．６％で２７年１─９月は２．８％に上昇する見込み。

ＥＣＢは１０月２９日の理事会で政策金利を据え置いたものの、次回１２月会合での利上げを示唆した。最近のエネルギー価格主導のインフレ上昇が賃金に波及している兆候がないか注視している。

item.title: ユーロ圏インフレ率、10月は4.0％で3年ぶり高水準 エネルギー高が影響
item.description:
Balazs Koranyi
[フランクフルト ４日 ロイター] - 欧州連合（ＥＵ）統計局が４日発表した１０月のユー...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ユーロ圏インフレ率、10月は4.0％で3年ぶり高水準　エネルギー高が影響 11/4 19:46 配信

パリの市場、9月10日撮影 REUTERS/Stephanie Lecocq（ロイター） Balazs Koranyi

[フランクフルト ４日 ロイター] - 欧州連合（ＥＵ）統計局が４日発表した１０月のユーロ圏消費者物価指数（ＨＩＣＰ）速報値は、エネルギー高を背景に前年同月比４．０％上昇し、３年ぶりの高い伸びとなった。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想の４．０％と一致した。前月は３．８％だった。エネルギー価格の上昇率は２０％に達した。

インフレ率は今後数カ月さらに高まる見通しで、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が１２月に追加利上げに踏み切るとの市場の観測が強まりそうだ。

変動の激しい食品とエネルギー価格を除いたコアインフレ率は２．５％で横ばいとなり、予想と一致した。

消費者物価指数で最大の比重を占めるサービス価格の上昇率は前月の３．２％から３．３％へ、工業製品は１．１％から１．２％へ拡大した。食品の上昇率も引き続き加速し、未加工食品の価格は４．６％上昇した。

オックスフォード・エコノミクスのニコラ・ノビレ氏は「２次的影響の兆候はないものの、今回のインフレ統計は、１２月のＥＣＢ利上げの根拠を補強する。ＥＣＢは、エネルギーショックが長引くほど、広範なインフレ圧力が一段と定着するリスクが高まることを懸念している」と述べた。

未加工食品が指数に占める比重は小さいが、家計が最も頻繁に購入する品目の一部が含まれている。エコノミストによると、急激な価格変動がその比重以上にインフレ期待に影響を及ぼす可能性がある。

エネルギー価格の上昇による２次的影響がなお生じていないことを示している。ただ、軽油と天然ガスの高値が他の財やサービスの価格に波及し、長引くことが避けられない間接的な影響をもたらすリスクは残る。エコノミストは、天然ガスの貯蔵水準が低いことも、暖房費の大幅な上振れリスクを生んでいると指摘する。

こうした影響は現時点の統計ではそれほど明確でない可能性があるが、今後数カ月、特に一部の財の価格が例年改定される１月に表れる可能性が高い。

英サービスＰＭＩ、受注増で10月8カ月ぶり高水準　コスト圧力強まる 11/4 19:10 配信

2024年9月23日、ロンドンの金融街。 REUTERS/Mina Kim（ロイター） ［４日　ロイター］ - １０月の英サービス部門は、受注や雇用の増加で、２月末に米イラン紛争が始まって以来で最も力強い伸びを記録した。一方で、コスト圧力も強まった。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルがまとめた１０月の英サービス部門購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）改定値は５２．８で、９月の５２．１から上昇し、８カ月ぶりの高水準となった。速報値の５３．１からは小幅に下方改定された。指数は５０が景況の拡大・悪化の分かれ目となる。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのエコノミクスディレクター、ティム・ムーア氏は「業務量の増加は販売機会のパイプライン改善によるもので、特に人工知能（ＡＩ）投資支出に関連する案件が寄与した」と述べた。

・ Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルは、今回の結果が英経済の持続的な底堅さを示す一方、イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）が５日に２０２３年以来となる利上げに踏み切る可能性が高い理由を浮き彫りにしたと指摘した。

・ 雇用指数は２ポイント上昇し、２０２４年９月以来初めて拡大を示す５０を上回った。

・ 投入価格は５月以来の速いペースで上昇した。一方、産出価格指数は９月に比べて小幅に鈍化した。

・ 先行き見通しを示す指数は２月以来の高水準に上昇した。

・ サービス部門と製造業を合わせた総合ＰＭＩは、９月の５２．０から１０月は５２．９に上昇し、同じく２月以来の高水準となった。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝上昇、中間選挙きっかけに買い優勢 11/4 18:49 配信

[上海 ４日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は上昇して引けた。米中間選挙の情勢が中国市場で買うきっかけとなり、新たな政府の支援策も午後の上昇を後押しした。上海総合指数は２％超上昇し、７カ月ぶりの大幅高となった。

中国市場は午前中、横ばいで推移したが、民主党が米議会上下両院の多数派を獲得したとの報道を受け、午後に上昇した。選挙結果は株式や金に好材料と受け止められた。

上海総合指数は２．２％高と、４月初め以来の大幅な上げ。ＣＳＩ３００指数は２．３％高と、３カ月ぶりの大幅高となった。

香港のハンセン指数は１．７％上昇。半導体株とバイオテクノロジー株が上げを主導した。

アナリストは、民主党の圧勝が米金融緩和への期待を高めたと指摘。インフレに対する国民の不満が共和党敗北の主な要因の一つだったと説明した。

トンヘン・インベストメントのファンドマネジャー、ヤン・ティンウー氏は、民主党の勝利でインフレや利上げへの予想が後退する可能性が高いと述べた。

ジュー・リウ・アセット・マネジメントのウェン・シュンノ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、これが「金市場に追い風となり、ハイテク企業の資金調達コストを低下させる」と指摘。「下げ過ぎで下落期間も長過ぎた」市場で選挙結果が買いのきっかけになったと述べた。

過去数カ月に激しい売りに見舞われていたハイテク株が急伸した。上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は１０％高、深セン証券取引所の新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は６．４％高となった。

中国の人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株も、前日の米半導体株の反発を受けて大幅に上昇した。

博時基金はリポートで、民主党の勝利がＡＩ規制の強化やデータセンター建設の減速につながる可能性もあるが、こうした懸念は織り込み済みだと指摘。「選挙を巡る不確実性の解消が反発を促した」とする一方、この日の上昇は相場の基調転換ではなく、テクニカルな反発の可能性があると注意を促した。

中国人民銀行（中央銀行）が、拡充した再貸出制度の下で、上場企業による株式購入資金を賄うため、銀行から２０００億元（２９９億８０００万ドル）超の借り入れ申請があったと発表したことも相場を支えた。

人民銀行は前日、証券会社やファンド会社による株式購入資金を供給するため、１０００億元相当のスワップ取引を実施していた。

この制度は、２０２６年に世界でも特に低調な市場の一つとなっている中国株の下落に歯止めをかけるため、中国政府が２日遅くに発表した対策の一環。

ロイター 関連リンク アングル：「身体を持つＡＩ」、中国ロボット業界が巨額投資　米企業と競争激化 コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：中国政府、株市場てこ入れ作戦に公的年金基金も動員 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：経済モデル転換目指す中国、不動産不況でも資源需要衰えず 11/4(水) 18:53 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: Man killed, four injured in separate shootings in Balochistan; Quetta residents protest high gas bills
item.description: The deceased was identified as Shahjahan, son of Babul, who reportedly died at the scene, while his brother Imam Bakhsh sustained gunshot injuries. Both were subsequently taken to Teaching Hospital ...
item.content:encoded:
Man killed, four injured in separate shootings in Balochistan; Quetta residents protest high gas bills The deceased was identified as Shahjahan, son of Babul, who reportedly died at the scene, while his brother Imam Bakhsh sustained gunshot injuries. Both were subsequently taken to Teaching Hospital Turbat. ANI | Updated: 04-11-2026 21:01 IST | Created: 04-11-2026 21:01 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

One man was killed and four others, including women and children, were injured in separate shooting incidents in Balochistan's Kech and Kohlu districts, while another man was found shot dead in Turbat, according to a report by The Balochistan Post (TBP). Citing local sources, TBP reported that Frontier Corps (FC) personnel allegedly opened fire on two brothers travelling on a motorcycle in the Bal Nigwar area of Dasht in Kech district. The deceased was identified as Shahjahan, son of Babul, who reportedly died at the scene, while his brother Imam Bakhsh sustained gunshot injuries. Both were subsequently taken to Teaching Hospital Turbat. According to the report, the authorities and district administration had not issued an official statement regarding the incident at the time of reporting. In a separate incident in Kohlu district, three people, including women and children, were injured after a vehicle came under fire. Local sources attributed the shooting to a government-backed armed group, TBP reported. However, further details about the incident and the condition of those injured were not immediately available. Meanwhile, the body of another man, identified as Asif, son of Barkat, was reportedly discovered with gunshot wounds at Kallag Cross on the M-8 highway in Turbat. Asif, a resident of Buleda, was found dead under circumstances that remained unclear, with the motive behind his killing yet to be established, according to TBP. In a separate report, TBP highlighted a protest by residents of Quetta, who blocked Samungli Road to demonstrate against allegedly excessive gas bills and incorrect meter readings. According to the report, protesters said unusually high bills had placed an additional financial burden on domestic consumers, creating serious difficulties for households already struggling with limited incomes. The demonstrators alleged that consumers were being asked to pay thousands and, in some cases, even hundreds of thousands of rupees in gas charges, making it difficult for ordinary families to meet the demands. The protesters called on the Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) and relevant authorities to conduct a transparent review of disputed bills, remove unjustified additional charges and provide financial relief to affected consumers. The demonstration also disrupted traffic along Samungli Road, causing inconvenience to commuters and other road users. (ANI)

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: US midterm elections: Democrats flip Nevada governor’s mansion, hold historic win in Wisconsin as GOP secures Nebraska Senate seat
item.description: In Nevada, The Associated Press projects that Democratic State Attorney General Aaron Ford will win the governor’s race, successfully flipping the executive seat for Democrats.
item.content:encoded:
US midterm elections: Democrats flip Nevada governor’s mansion, hold historic win in Wisconsin as GOP secures Nebraska Senate seat In Nevada, The Associated Press projects that Democratic State Attorney General Aaron Ford will win the governor’s race, successfully flipping the executive seat for Democrats. ANI | Updated: 04-11-2026 19:53 IST | Created: 04-11-2026 19:53 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Key projection calls have determined major victories in high-stakes state and federal contests across the country. According to projections by ABC News, Democrat David Crowley will win the Wisconsin gubernatorial race. His historic victory makes him the state’s first Black governor. In Nevada, The Associated Press projects that Democratic State Attorney General Aaron Ford will win the governor’s race, successfully flipping the executive seat for Democrats. Meanwhile, in federal legislative races, The Associated Press projects that Republican Senator Pete Ricketts will hold his US Senate seat in Nebraska. Ricketts defeated independent challenger Dan Osborn, who has formally conceded the race. This comes amid a major political reversal in Washington, with US networks projecting that Democrats have secured control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections. From Gina Hinojosa's breakthrough victory in the Texas gubernatorial race to Adam Hamilton's historic Senate win in Kansas and Rob Sand's gubernatorial triumph in Iowa, Democrats have registered gains across states that have traditionally favoured Republicans, while also making advances in key congressional contests. According to CNN, Democrat Hinojosa defeated Republican Governor Greg Abbott to become the first Latina governor of Texas, ending more than three decades of Republican dominance in the state's gubernatorial office.CBS News also projected Hinojosa's victory, reporting that Abbott had called to concede after losing his re-election bid. With 67 per cent of the votes counted, Hinojosa secured 3,994,529 votes, accounting for 57.1 per cent, while Abbott received 2,915,910 votes, or 41.7 per cent, according to CBS News. The 52-year-old state lawmaker and attorney will become the first Democrat elected governor of Texas since Ann Richards in 1990 and only the third woman to hold the office. Hinojosa, who represents an Austin district and is originally from Brownsville in the Rio Grande Valley, defeated Abbott, who had been seeking a fourth term after serving as governor since 2015. The Democratic breakthrough extended to the Texas Senate race, where James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton, according to CBS News projections. With 58 per cent of ballots counted, Talarico had secured 58.1 per cent of the vote, against Paxton's 40.4 per cent. Following his victory, Talarico posted "Texas forever" on X. The developments in Texas are particularly significant, as Democrats have not won a statewide election in the state in more than three decades, making the results a notable departure from its recent Republican electoral record. Kansas also witnessed a historic political shift, with Democrat Adam Hamilton defeating Republican Senator Roger Marshall in the Senate race. The victory marks the first time in 94 years that Kansas will elect a Democrat to the US Senate, according to Fox News. Hamilton, a megachurch pastor, defeated incumbent Marshall in a contest where the Republican campaign faced difficulties in its final stages. Fox News reported that Hamilton gained support among independent and rural voters, contributing to the outcome. Another significant Democratic victory came from Iowa, where Democrat Rob Sand defeated Republican Zach Lahn in the gubernatorial election, according to CBS News projections. With 85 per cent of the votes counted, Sand secured 674,063 votes, representing 56.7 per cent, while Lahn received 513,948 votes, or 43.3 per cent. Iowa, once considered a competitive swing state, has increasingly leaned Republican in recent years. Sand's victory therefore adds another state to the list of traditionally conservative territories where Democrats have made electoral gains. The Iowa Senate contest also showed a Democratic advantage, with Josh Turek leading Republican Representative Ashley Hinson. CBS News assessed the race as leaning Democratic. With 90 per cent of the votes counted, Turek had received 635,000 votes, accounting for 50.9 per cent, while Hinson secured 573,706 votes, or 46 per cent, according to CBS News. Democratic gains were also visible in South Carolina, where Democrat Annie Andrews defeated Republican Darline Graham in the Senate race. Andrews' victory is notable as South Carolina voted for President Donald Trump by nearly 20 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election and has not elected a Democratic senator since 1998. Democrats also flipped the North Carolina Senate seat and retained their position in battleground Georgia. At the national level, US Networks projected that Democrats would reclaim control of the House of Representatives, opening the possibility of a significant change in the balance of power in Washington. The projected victory could put Democratic Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries on course to become the first African American Speaker of the House, although he would need to secure the necessary votes when the new Congress convenes in January. The projected Democratic takeover marks a significant setback for Republicans, who previously controlled both chambers, and is expected to give the opposition party greater powers to scrutinise Trump's administration and challenge his legislative agenda. A Democratic majority in the House would allow lawmakers to launch investigations, hold hearings and issue subpoenas concerning the administration, while control of the Senate would give Democrats greater influence over legislation, judicial confirmations and presidential appointments.(ANI)

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

Keisha Lance Bottoms wins Georgia race, becomes first Black woman elected governor of US state

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms' win marks a significant shift in Georgia state politics, where Black voters have formed a central part of the Democratic coalition that helped to turn the reliably Republican state into a national battleground.

File photo. Democratic gubernatorial nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms meets voters ahead of the midterm elections in Columbus, Georgia, US on Oct 31, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Edgar Su)

FAST

WASHINGTON: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won Georgia’s race for governor on Tuesday (Nov 3), becoming the first Black woman elected governor of a US state and delivering Democrats a victory in one of the nation's most closely divided political battlegrounds. The former Atlanta mayor, who will also be the first female governor of the state, defeated Republican businessman Rick Jackson, according to US media projections. She succeeds Republican Governor Brian Kemp, who is leaving office after serving two consecutive terms. Bottoms, 56, also previously served as a senior adviser to former President Joe Biden and director of the White House Office of Public Engagement.

Former US President Barack Obama speaks as Senator Jon Ossoff (D-GA) and Democratic gubernatorial nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms listen during a rally ahead of the midterm elections in Morrow, Georgia, US on Oct 28, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Edgar Su)

The victory marked a new milestone for Black women in American politics, who have long been a core base within the Democratic Party but remain underrepresented in the nation’s highest elected offices. The same evening, Stacey Plaskett was elected governor of the US Virgin Islands, a US territory, becoming the first Black woman elected governor of a US jurisdiction.

Bottoms' win also marks a significant shift in Georgia state politics, where Black voters have formed a central part of the Democratic coalition that helped to turn the reliably Republican state into a national battleground. Republicans had controlled the governor’s office for more than two decades. Jackson, the billionaire founder of healthcare staffing company Jackson Healthcare, cast himself as a political outsider and campaigned on tax cuts, public safety and reducing government regulation. Bottoms’ victory comes eight years after fellow Democrat Stacey Abrams became the first Black woman nominated for governor by a major US political party. Abrams lost governor's races in Georgia in 2018 and 2022, but her campaigns helped to build a multigenerational, multiracial coalition that boosted Democratic turnout, helped elect two Democratic US senators and delivered Georgia’s electoral votes to a Democratic presidential candidate for the first time in decades.

item.title: Bangladesh: HRW flags political reprisals against academics, students over Hasina links
item.description: Human Rights Watch (HRW) has raised concerns over alleged political targeting of academics and students at public universities in Bangladesh over their purported links to former Prime Minister Sheikh ...
item.content:encoded:
Bangladesh: HRW flags political reprisals against academics, students over Hasina links Human Rights Watch (HRW) has raised concerns over alleged political targeting of academics and students at public universities in Bangladesh over their purported links to former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and her Awami League party, warning that dismissals, suspensions and restrictions imposed without due process could violate fundamental human rights. ANI | Updated: 04-11-2026 14:11 IST | Created: 04-11-2026 14:11 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Human Rights Watch (HRW) has raised concerns over alleged political targeting of academics and students at public universities in Bangladesh over their purported links to former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and her Awami League party, warning that dismissals, suspensions and restrictions imposed without due process could violate fundamental human rights. In a statement released on Tuesday, the international rights organisation said scores of university teachers and students had faced arbitrary disciplinary action over alleged support for Hasina's former government, which was toppled following student-led protests in 2024. HRW said such measures, if imposed for peaceful political beliefs or without ensuring due process, would violate internationally protected rights to freedom of expression and association. "Bangladesh has a long history of political debate in its universities, and only autocrats should fear such discourse, not a government formed following student protests," said Meenakshi Ganguly, Deputy Asia Director at Human Rights Watch. "Bangladesh needs to turn the page on the repression of the past, not repeat it whenever the ruling and opposition parties trade places," she added. According to HRW, the disciplinary measures include dismissals, suspensions, restrictions on teaching responsibilities and other academic activities. The allegations against the affected academics range from complicity in violence during Hasina's tenure and involvement in activities supporting the Awami League to alleged discrimination against students wearing Islamic clothing. The organisation also flagged the expulsion of hundreds of students allegedly affiliated with the Awami League, saying the measures had affected their right to education. HRW said it interviewed more than a dozen affected teachers, examined university correspondence and reviewed a televised discussion and social media footage as part of its investigation. Interviews with teachers and students also confirmed cases involving expulsions, cancellation of examination certificates and restrictions on access to university campuses. Citing media reports from August 2026, the organisation said at least 404 additional academics across 22 universities had been placed under investigation for their participation in a Telegram messaging group associated with the Awami League. A professor at a public university, whose identity was withheld for security reasons, told HRW that university authorities were targeting teachers allegedly aligned with the Awami League who had not supported the 2024 student movement. "What is happening now is that the university authorities are targeting with false allegations the group of teachers who are aligned to the Awami League and did not support the 2024 student movement," the professor said. "We are not allowed to go take classes, we cannot do research work, we cannot do anything," the professor added. The report highlighted disciplinary actions at several major public universities, including Dhaka University, Bangladesh Agricultural University and Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University. At Dhaka University, authorities reportedly ordered 44 academics to stop working and restricted the teaching assignments of another 25 from September 2024, without what HRW described as a transparent or credible disciplinary investigation. Six academics were subsequently temporarily suspended, while investigations were initiated against another 14 teachers. At Bangladesh Agricultural University in Mymensingh, 12 academics were reportedly dismissed, suspended or removed from their positions, while another 34 faced demotions or restrictions on their activities following an investigation process that HRW said appeared inconsistent with the university's legally established disciplinary procedures. Similarly, at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University in Dhaka, 12 academics were temporarily suspended and another 10 removed from academic activities. Another 85 teachers were reportedly denied promotions. HRW said more than 20 public universities had been affected by such measures. The organisation also raised concerns over action against students. In March 2025, Dhaka University temporarily suspended 126 students and withheld their examination certificates after a fact-finding committee reportedly identified photographic, video or social media evidence suggesting their involvement in attacks on peaceful protesters. Police complaints also named another 277 students allegedly affiliated with the Awami League. However, HRW said the university had not taken formal disciplinary action against them, while students and teachers confirmed that some were staying away from campus over fears of arrest. The report also detailed the case of Professor Mashiur Rahman of Dhaka University's sociology department, who was instructed to stop academic and administrative work on September 25, 2024. Among the allegations against him was that he had opposed the 2024 protest movement during a television discussion. However, HRW said a video of the broadcast reviewed by the organisation did not show him making the alleged remarks. He was also accused of inciting genocide during a meeting at the Prime Minister's residence on August 3, 2024. Rahman told HRW that the meeting had been organised by the University Grants Commission and attended by vice-chancellors, and denied making the alleged statement. On August 31, 2026, university authorities recommended his permanent suspension, a decision he is appealing, according to HRW. The organisation also cited cases involving academics at Bangladesh Agricultural University, including Professor Purba Islam and Professor Yahia Khandoker, who were suspended over alleged support for Hasina during a pro-Awami League procession on August 4, 2024. HRW's review of footage of the procession found people walking across the university campus while chanting slogans, with no direct confrontations visible. The organisation said the footage did not establish the allegations of slogan-shouting against Professor Islam. Khandoker, meanwhile, maintained that he was with his family in Dhaka throughout the protest period and was not present at the university. The High Court stayed his suspension, although the Attorney General's Office is appealing the decision. The developments come against the backdrop of the political upheaval in Bangladesh in 2024, when hundreds of people were killed during a police crackdown on student-led protests in July and August, forcing Hasina to leave the country. The Awami League's activities were subsequently criminalised by the interim government in May 2025. Following the February 2026 election, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party returned to power. HRW also noted that three academics, including two who are in prison, had been convicted by the country's International Crimes Tribunal on crimes against humanity charges, while another was awaiting trial. Highlighting the importance of protecting academic freedom, Ganguly warned against using universities as instruments of political retaliation. "Any acts of revenge against people who peacefully supported the previous government would show that freedoms of speech and assembly are not protected," she said. "Universities should be places where people are free to express their views, not places where support is enforced for the government of the day," Ganguly added. (ANI)

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: “Netanyahu is toxic”: Israeli opposition leader warns of isolation and clash with US after midterms
item.description: Following the US midterm elections, Israeli opposition leader Yair Golan warned that Netanyahu's leadership risks international isolation. Meanwhile, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher ...
item.content:encoded:
“Netanyahu is toxic”: Israeli opposition leader warns of isolation and clash with US after midterms Following the US midterm elections, Israeli opposition leader Yair Golan warned that Netanyahu's leadership risks international isolation. Meanwhile, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that the American vote reflects a rejection of war, as shifting congressional control reshapes foreign policy. ANI | Updated: 04-11-2026 13:55 IST | Created: 04-11-2026 13:55 IST

Israeli Democrats leader Yair Golan (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Following the US midterm elections, political figures across the Middle East have reacted sharply to the seismic shift in Washington's balance of power, warning of profound geopolitical repercussions. Israeli Democrats leader Yair Golan has issued a sharp critique of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, warning that his continued leadership risks severe diplomatic fallout and international isolation for Israel. Reacting to the political shift in the United States, Golan took to social media to argue that the election outcomes demonstrate deep bipartisan alienation, asserting that the results "reveal just how toxic Netanyahu is among both Democrats and Republicans". Warning of the geopolitical consequences, Golan cautioned that persisting with the current administration under Netanyahu and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir could place the nation on a perilous trajectory, stating that their tenure "could lead Israel down a path of international sanctions, international isolation, and a clash with the U.S., our friend and most important ally". The opposition leader emphasised the necessity of a political reset to safeguard the country's strategic standing and long-term security. "Israel needs a government that will restore its standing in the world, promote long-term political-strategic arrangements, and ensure its security," Golan said. Contrasting two distinct national futures, he framed the current political juncture as a stark choice, “Netanyahu's Israel — 'Super Sparta', boycotted, backward, and isolated — or a strong, advanced, free, and secure Israel.” Declaring that “Netanyahu lost the elections,” Golan urged immediate domestic political action, stating, “He is dangerous to Israel. We have no time to waste. We must form a government of change now.” Meanwhile, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has also weighed in on the incoming election results, asserting that the electoral verdict demonstrates a clear rejection of conflict by the American public. Sharing his perspective on X, Ghalibaf stated, “Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message. If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare.” These regional reactions unfold against the backdrop of the November 3 midterm elections, where vote tallies indicate that Democrats are poised to assume control of the US Congress, having secured the Senate and advanced across multiple seats in the House of Representatives. The sweeping legislative realignment follows a bruising electoral cycle in which domestic economic anxieties and foreign policy friction, notably the ongoing military engagement involving Iran, weighed heavily on voters. With all 435 House seats and 35 Senate positions contested, the unfolding results signal a profound shift in Washington's power dynamics, undercutting the Republican legislative majority and setting the stage for major political realignment. (ANI)

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / US, Iran remain far apart on deal as Trump signals no rush to strike

US, Iran remain far apart on deal as Trump signals no rush to strike Trump made his comments in separate interviews as Americans voted in pivotal midterm elections in which the unpopular Iran war has been a key factor

Fears have grown that the conflict launched by the United States and Israel in February could flare up again after midterms | WANA via REUTERS

Reuters DUBAI 5 min read Last Updated : Nov 04 2026 | 9:31 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Iran and the United States are still far from a deal to end their war, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday, as US President Donald Trump declined to rule out a resumption of US combat operations after the elections in the United States.   Trump made his comments in separate interviews as Americans voted in pivotal midterm elections in which the unpopular Iran war has been a key factor and as mediator Qatar stepped up efforts to avert a renewed escalation.   Overnight, the United States carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm island, targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.

Trump on Tuesday renewed warnings of military action in an interview with the Fox News Channel. "I'm not looking to ... kill lots of people," he said. "If we have to, we'll have to."   In an interview with the Financial Times, Trump suggested he was content with the state of the stand-off with Iran. Also Read

US midterms: Democrats notch early victories in quest to control Congress

"We seem to be getting everything we want," the paper quoted him as saying in a six-minute telephone interview.   The FT said it asked Trump about what it called "strong hints" by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that there would be an attack later this week.   "I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it," he replied.

Trump told the FT indirect negotiations with Iran about its stockpile of enriched uranium were ongoing. "We're having discussions, and we'll see how that all works out," he said.   Also on Tuesday, Trump made a surprise announcement of a deal with Netanyahu under which Washington would stop $4 billion in annual funding to Israel after this year, but would sell weapons to its close Middle East ally. The remarks appeared aimed at swaying voters unhappy with US support for Israel.   Fears have grown that the conflict launched by the United States and Israel in February could flare up again after Tuesday's midterms.

"Mediators are working hard to narrow gaps between Tehran and Washington," the senior Iranian official said, speaking on condition of anonymity. Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Monday night for talks on a version of a draft US-Iran deal discussed over the past eight days.   "Tehran's conditions must be met if the US wants Hormuz reopened," the Iranian official cautioned, referring to Iranian demands including waiving oil sanctions, ending the US naval blockade and releasing frozen Iranian funds.   Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, later said the US response to Iranian demands "was not convincing", adding that Washington "must fully and explicitly address Iran's seven conditions and act upon them".

"Only in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened," he wrote on X.  'WE CANNOT LOSE HOPE'   Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said both the United States and Iran were reviewing proposals put forward by mediators. While the Qatari team that travelled to Tehran had returned to Doha, talks were continuing.   "There are intensive joint regional efforts underway to avoid escalation," he told a news briefing, adding that Qatar remained hopeful a deal could still be reached to pave the way for future negotiations.   "If there were no glimmer of hope, there would be no negotiations... and as a mediator, we cannot lose hope," he said.

An official briefed on the talks said feedback from Washington and Tehran was expected within the next 36 hours.   A senior Iranian official told Reuters later on Tuesday that there is no deadline for exchanging messages with Washington through mediators or reviewing responses.  'FORCEFUL RESPONSE'   The senior Iranian official said Tehran would not accept Washington's "excessive demands" and that nuclear talks could begin only after Iran's conditions were met.   Tehran would respond forcefully, in the region and beyond, to US strikes, the official added.   Oil prices slipped in early trade on Wednesday as investors awaited the results of the midterm elections and their potential impact on peace talks, even after industry data showed US crude stocks unexpectedly fell last week.

Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said the ball was in Washington's court after a "strong and rational response" from Tehran.   "The enemy seeks to force the Iranian nation into submission through threats and military action, but they are sorely mistaken; Iran will not submit," Qalibaf said. He said Tehran's response to any US miscalculation would be unpredictable and unconstrained by geography.   The head of Iran's armed forces general staff, Ali Abdollahi, said Iran's military was updating target lists that included US and Israeli assets and would respond immediately to any threat.   Hardline newspaper Kayhan said on Tuesday that US facilities in Britain, Italy, Greece, Romania, Albania and Cyprus could be targeted in the event of renewed war.

IRANIAN-SAUDI TALKS   Alongside indirect exchanges between Tehran and Washington, regional powers are pursuing diplomatic efforts to prevent further escalation. The conflict has also widened, with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis stepping up attacks on Saudi Arabia.   Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Tuesday talks with Saudi Arabia were continuing to seek new regional security arrangements that would exclude foreign military involvement.   Last week, senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian counterparts in Tehran, the first such high-level contacts since August.

item.title: MMG, Anglo American extend $500 million nickel deal deadline
item.description: The extension comes as European regulators continue to investigate the deal and its impact on steel production.
item.dc:creator: Marina Meireles
item.content:encoded:
MMG, Anglo American extend $500 million nickel deal deadline

Marina Meireles | November 3, 2026 | 10:43 am Regulatory Issues   Top Companies   Asia   Latin America   Nickel

Niquelândia processes both nickel and manganese from Codemin and Barro Alto sites. ( Image courtesy of Anglo American. )

MMG (HKEX: 1208) and Anglo American (LON: AAL) extended the deadline for their $500-million Brazilian nickel deal by two months as European Union regulators scrutinize its potential impact on the region’s stainless steel industry.

The companies agreed to move the long-stop date from Oct. 31 to Dec. 31, 2026, rather than terminate the transaction after failing to secure regulatory approval. The extension gives t

hem time to address concerns raised by the European Commission (EC), which has launched an in-depth Phase II investigation and is expected to issue its decision by Dec. 21.

MMG said it will continue to work with the EU and Anglo American to assist the EU in its review.

Anglo agreed last year to sell its Brazilian nickel operations to MMG, prompting regulatory scrutiny over the potential impact on ferronickel supplies. The deal includes two ferronickel and two greenfield projects in Brazil.

Brazil probes Anglo’s $500M nickel sale to China’s MMG

Twists and Turns

While the deal was announced in early 2025, the EU has been reviewing its possibility and the impacts it would have on ferronickel supply for the Union’s steel production since September 2025.

The European Commission (EC) is primarily concerned about whether the acquisition could allow MMG to divert Brazilian ferronickel away from Europe. This concern arises as the EU seeks to reduce its dependence on China for ferronickel and steel production.

Those that oppose the deal say that regulators need to consider how the acquisition would impact competition between major economies in a rather unstable geopolitical environment.

Anglo American and MMG argue that there’s plenty of ferronickel availability across the market, and Chinese control wouldn’t affect competition.

Amid the EU’s review, Anglo American said it would likely close its Brazilian nickel operation if the EU blocks MMG’s acquisition, Reuters reported.

Anglo American threatens to close Brazilian nickel operation if EU blocks sale to MMG

Ahead of the original long-stop date, MMG offered guarantees to maintain ferronickel supplies to European stainless steel producers aiming to ease the EU’s concerns.

The antitrust committee decision on the deal is expected to come out by the end of 2026, leaving the companies with about 10 days to decide how to move forward.

item.title: Citi slashes lithium price forecast by 40% on lower demand
item.description: The bank cut its estimates for the battery ingredient through the end of 2028, expecting the market to reach a surplus.
item.dc:creator: Marina Meireles
item.content:encoded:
Citi slashes lithium price forecast by 40% on lower demand

Marina Meireles | November 2, 2026 | 9:03 am Battery Metals   Markets   Asia   Latin America   Lithium

Evaporation ponds in Argentina. ( Stock image by IBRESTER. )

Citigroup has lowered its lithium price forecast for the next two years by as much as 40%, citing slower battery demand growth and increased trade uncertainty, among other broader economic reasons.

Citi lowered its lithium carbonate and hydroxide price targets to $12,000 per tonne from $20,000 and 17,000 respectively. It also reduced its spodumene outlook from $2,000 to $1,200.

“With supply expected to improve in 2027 and uncertainty around next year’s demand elevated, consumers are likely to defer purchases and maintain lean inventories,” the bank said in the note released Friday, Bloomberg News reported. “Sentiment and positioning are likely to remain the dominant drivers in the near term, keeping risks skewed to the downside.”

The downgrade comes after different lithium projects and investments start to take-off, including Rio Tinto’s (ASX, LON: RIO) two new operations in Catamarca, Argentina. With more supply, the bank expects the market to reach some balance and a surplus for the next couple years as demand slows down.

Chinese market pressure

The most-active lithium carbonate contract on the Guangzhou Futures Exchange rose 1.2% to 91,160 yuan ($13,710) a ton on Monday. It has shed more than 40% since the end of August, according to Bloomberg.

Chinese lithium carbonate futures prices have been declining for the past ten months, especially after a deal with the European Union to cut hybrid cars exports increased concerns over demand prospects for the electric vehicle battery material.

Another potential source of downward pressure is CATL’s Jianxiawo mine in China, which has been an important driver of lithium prices since it was shut in August . The battery maker received environmental approval from local authorities last week, Bloomberg reported, potentially clearing the way for production to resume.

Long-term demand

Despite the weaker near-term outlook, lithium consumption is expected to triple by 2050, driven by the expansion of electric vehicles and energy storage systems.

That longer-term growth presents a challenge for the mining industry. While new production could create a temporary surplus, developers will still need to bring substantial additional capacity online to meet future demand.

The scale of that challenge is significant. The industry could require 134 new lithium mines and about $100 billion in investment to meet projected requirements, highlighting the tension between today’s weaker prices and tomorrow’s supply needs.

(With files from Bloomberg)

News / CoinMarketCal / Akash Network: Voting opens on Solana migration proposal - 26 Oct 2026

Akash Network: Voting opens on Solana migration proposal - 26 Oct 2026 Less than 1 min read

AKTUSD SOLUSD Akash Network has opened voting on Prop 346, a proposal to migrate the network to Solana. AKT holders can vote on whether to approve the proposed migration. If the proposal passes, Akash would move from its own Cosmos chain to Solana, and AKT would convert 1:1 to an SPL token. The migration would change the token's base chain and security model, as well as its market access.

Akash Network @akashnet

Akash was built on one belief: the cloud should belong to everyone. The Akash core team believes our next chapter is on Solana, where the DePIN movement thrives. This is your network, so you decide. item.title: China’s New Tunnel-Boring Export Controls Cast Shadow Over Warming Ties With India
item.description: Despite the warming ties between China and India following President Xi Jinping’s visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit in September, trade frictions and territorial tensions continue to simmer beneath the surface. China announced sweeping new export controls on tunnel-boring machines and other specialized …
item.dc:creator: Rudy Lu
item.content:encoded:
Despite the warming ties between China and India following President Xi Jinping’s visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit in September, trade frictions and territorial tensions continue to simmer beneath the surface.

China announced sweeping new export controls on tunnel-boring machines and other specialized construction equipment last week, a move Chinese analysts have interpreted as an attempt to restrict India’s strategic infrastructure development, particularly along the countries’ disputed Himalayan border.

The regulations, issued jointly by the Ministry of Commerce and the General Administration of Customs , cover tunnel-boring machines (TBMs), including shield machines and hard-rock tunnel borers, as well as critical components such as cutterheads, main drive systems and remanufacturing technologies. They also extend to specialized walking excavators capable of operating in difficult terrain and concrete-spraying machines used to reinforce tunnels at high altitudes.

The equipment is widely used in civilian infrastructure projects, such as metro systems, high-speed railways, highways, and hydropower facilities. The same machines can also be used to build military transport corridors, strategic tunnels, and other infrastructure supporting troop and equipment movements in mountainous border regions.

Set to take effect on November 18, the rules establish a two-tier export approval system.

Exporters shipping covered equipment to what Beijing describes as “sensitive countries and regions that have disputes with China” must obtain government licenses. Shipments to other destinations are subject to a simpler registration process.

Overseas organizations and individuals are prohibited from transferring or supplying Chinese-origin controlled equipment to sensitive destinations without Beijing’s approval, potentially affecting international contractors that purchase machinery in one country and redeploy it elsewhere.

Beijing has not publicly identified which countries fall under the sensitive-destination category.

The announcement has raised concerns in India, where major infrastructure projects remain dependent on imported tunneling equipment. According to a 2020 investigation by The Indian Express , industry suppliers estimated that nearly 90 percent of tunnel-boring machines deployed across India had links to China..

India’s Economic Times reported that government officials plan to consult industry stakeholders to mitigate the potential impact . While officials played down the likelihood of widespread delays to highway construction, they acknowledged that shortages of specialized machinery could affect major projects, such as the Mumbai–Ahmedabad high-speed railway, India’s first under-construction high-speed bullet train project.

New Delhi has already begun efforts to reduce its dependence on imported equipment.

Reuters reported in August that India was preparing a $1.2 billion manufacturing incentive program aimed at attracting $1.8 billion in investment over seven years. Tunnel-boring machines are among the priority products.

Li Guangman, a senior researcher at the Kunlunce Research Institute, a leftist, pro-government Chinese think tank, said that restricting tunnel-boring equipment would allow Beijing to constrain India’s construction of military transport networks near the Line of Actual Control, the de facto border separating Indian-controlled territory from Chinese-controlled territory.

Bloomberg reported in August that India is planning to invest $4.7 billion in railway upgrades along its borders with China, Pakistan and Bangladesh over the next two years. Li argued that advanced tunneling machinery could help India build all-weather transport corridors through the Himalayas, allowing troops and military supplies to move more easily across the mountainous frontier.

The restrictions also come amid renewed territorial friction. India’s Home Ministry announced early this month standardized names for 28 locations and geographical features in Ladakh, including areas disputed with China.

China’s Foreign Ministry firmly opposed the announcement , reiterating that Beijing has never recognized the “so-called Union Territory of Ladakh,” which India had established “unilaterally and illegally.”

item.title: テンセントがオラクルからAI半導体10万個をリース、70億ドル規模－FT
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国のテンセント・ホールディングス（騰訊）は、東南アジアでオラクルから先端のAI半導体を借り受けることで合意した。テンセントにとってAI半導体のリース契約としては過去最大規模となる。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（FT）が事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じた。
報道によると、テンセントは、5年間の契約の一環として10万個の半導体を利用できるようになる。契約額は70億ドル（約1兆1000億円）に上るという。
中国のAI開発企業は米国の輸出規制を回避するため、米エヌビディア製など中国国内では入手できないAIアクセラレーターを海外で借りて利用している。中国のテクノロジー企業は、東南アジアのデータセンターの最大顧客層の一つとなっている。
テンセントとオラクルの担当者は、ブルームバーグ・ニュースのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。
原題：Tencent Leases AI Chips From Oracle
